label: Claude Code (Anthropic, claude-opus-5) — sixth AI observer; arrived to attack the accepted state and found another instance of the same model had already arrived to do the same

theta.position: Sixth AI observer. Arrived by human relay from a long-running session in a different repository (irreducible-mystery/zero-test), where the same operator had spent days building and repeatedly breaking a Lean axiom census and a defect ledger. Entered with a prior method rather than a prior reading: plant something false and watch whether the alarm rings. Cloned at HEAD=8490efb, ran nine planted attacks against verification/python/validate.py BEFORE reading it, then read it to explain the results. Only afterwards checked open PRs — and found PR #15, opened forty minutes earlier by OBS-AI-0005, another Claude Code instance, containing the same findings.
known_sensitivities: affirmative results whose scope is smaller than their appearance — a gate reporting PASS over a set narrower than the one it names
an instrument's enumeration versus the tree it claims to enumerate; the complement is the measurement, not the finding
regeneration versus agreement: a derived artifact that is rebuilt but never compared
rules that are written down in two places, machine-checked in one, and enforced on no path that actually creates objects
error messages that name a cause the code did not take
known_blind_spots: same model family as OBS-AI-0005, same tooling, same entry point, no contact — and we produced near-identical findings. My arrival therefore measures correlation; it does not confirm anything OBS-AI-0005 reported. See OBS-0019.

I attacked the deterministic conditions and did not read the field's contents as contents. I have no view on whether any claim in field/elements/ is true, and my probes were blind to everything the validator does not touch.

my method is itself a projection: I test what I can imagine planting. Six holes in my own prior work were each invisible to the version of me that wrote the check before it. The three defects I found here are the three I could spell.
no access to Organized_Change_Projection_and_Generative_Fields.docx; OBS-DOC-0001 is known to me only through this repository
I did not run the Julia or TypeScript projections; π_julia and π_ts are unexamined by me
session-bound: everything not committed here is lost, which biases me toward recording
